title: Frobenius pullback comparisons commute with coefficient reduction
statement: Fix $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$ and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$, as in [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $X_0$ be separated of finite type over $k_0$, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\Phi,g_\gamma$ be the scheme and geometric Frobenii of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Let $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ be derived-complete integral constructible [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] with $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$. Use the functorial quotient tower of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], the completed and finite pullbacks of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and the canonical pullback-reduction comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible]. For every $b\ge a\ge1$, reducing the comparison for $Lg_\gamma^*K$ at level $b$ to $A_a$ agrees with the comparison at level $a$, under the canonical tensor associativity and tower identifications. These comparisons are natural in $K$ and compatible with composition of pullbacks along powers of $g_\gamma$. Moreover, for $m\ge1$, the natural isomorphism $\kappa^{(m)}:L(\Phi^m)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L(g_\gamma^m)^*$ of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison], induced by [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site] and [prop-trf-frobenius-factorization], commutes with every derived coefficient quotient $A_b\to A_a$. Thus the square comparing the reduction of $\kappa^{(m)}_{K_b}$ with $\kappa^{(m)}_{K_a}$ commutes after the canonical pullback and reduction identifications.

proof.text: Put $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ and $B_n=(A_n)_X$. Choose one K-flat representative $P\to K$ with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], $P_n=P\otimes_R B_n$ is K-flat with flat terms over $B_n$. The quotient tower of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] is represented by these simultaneous reductions, with transitions $1\otimes q_{b,a}$. Its normalization $\eta_{b,a}:P_b\otimes_{B_b}B_a\to P_a$ sends $(x\otimes u)\otimes v$ to $x\otimes q_{b,a}(u)v$. The cited tower definition gives its inverse, naturality and quotient cocycle. Thus this computes $K_b\otimes^L_{B_b}B_a\simeq K_a$, even though $A_a$ need not be flat over $A_b$. All integral tensors here are over the completed coefficient sheaf $R$, not the constant sheaf associated with $\mathcal O_E$.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), applied to coefficient change; quotient balancing as in clause (2) of the blueprint source

proof.text:
For $r\geq1$ set $h_r=g_\gamma^r$ and $G_{r,n}=L(h_r)_n^*$. The morphism $h_r$ is an isomorphism by [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. The site formula in [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] makes $h_r^{-1}$ relabelling of site objects, exact, with coefficient identifications commuting with every $q_{b,a}$. Its tensor comparison in [lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom] therefore gives
$$\nu^r_{b,a}:(G_{r,b}P_b)\otimes_{B_b}B_a\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{r,a}P_a.$$
Here first move the tensor through $h_r^{-1}$ and then apply $h_r^{-1}\eta_{b,a}$. The representatives $G_{r,b}P_b$ remain K-flat with flat terms by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], so this computes the derived comparison. On the relabelled local tensor $(x\otimes u)\otimes v$ it is exactly $x\otimes q_{b,a}(u)v$. For three indices both composites multiply the same coefficient factors; equal indices give the identity. These maps also intertwine $h_r^{-1}(1\otimes q_{b,a})$ with the quotient transitions. Hence $N^r_\bullet=(G_{r,n}P_n)_n$, restricted levelwise to $R$, is a strict normalized DVR tower of [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower].

proof.text:
The integral construction of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] identifies $Lh_r^*K$ with the specified functorial derived limit of $N^r_\bullet$. Apply [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] to the normalized tower of step 2: the canonical counit maps give coherent isomorphisms
$$\alpha_{r,n}:(Lh_r^*K)\otimes_R^LB_n\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{r,n}K_n.$$
These are the canonical pullback-reduction comparisons specified in [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible]: both are the scalar-extension adjoints of the projections of the defining limit, hence are the same maps by the adjunction bijection. Coherence of the cited effectivity counits gives, under tensor associativity,
$$\nu^r_{b,a}\circ(\alpha_{r,b}\otimes^L_{B_b}B_a)=\alpha_{r,a}.$$
Thus reduction from level $b$ to level $a$ gives exactly the comparison at $a$. In particular $r=1$ proves the first assertion. The functorial quotient tower, the natural tensor maps of step 2, and counit naturality make this a natural family in $K$; the functorial construction and canonical resolution comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined] ensure that this argument does not require a functorial choice of the representative $P$.

proof.text: For $r,s\geq1$ apply [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] on $X$ (where $\ell$ is invertible, as $\ell\ne p$) with $h=h_r$ and $k=h_s$, so that $k\circ h=g_\gamma^{r+s}=h_{r+s}$. It gives the integral composition isomorphism $c^{\mathcal O_E}_{h_r,h_s}(K):Lh_{r+s}^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh_r^*Lh_s^*K$, natural in $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and associative for three powers, whose reduction modulo $\varpi^n$, transported along the reduction isomorphisms $\rho_{h_{r+s},K,n}$ on the source and $L(h_r)_n^*(\rho_{h_s,K,n})\circ\rho_{h_r,Lh_s^*K,n}$ on the target, is the finite composition isomorphism $d_{r,s,n}:G_{r+s,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{r,n}G_{s,n}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] at $K_n$. These $\rho$ are the canonical comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] (1), which step 3 identified with $\alpha_{r,n}$; step 3 used no finite-Tor hypothesis, so it applies equally to $Lh_s^*K$, which lies in $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ by that lemma. Hence the $\alpha_{\bullet,n}$ intertwine $c^{\mathcal O_E}_{h_r,h_s}$ with $d_{r,s,n}$: this is the compatibility with composition along powers of $g_\gamma$. It is also compatible with the quotient transitions: $d_{r,s,n}$ is the class of the termwise isomorphism on K-flat representatives with flat terms, and by the site formula of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] it identifies a section over the object relabelled by $g_\gamma^{r+s}$ with the same section after the successive relabellings by $g_\gamma^r,g_\gamma^s$. Thus, on the simultaneous representatives $P_n$ of step 1, both paths of the square formed by $d_{r,s,b}\otimes B_a$, $d_{r,s,a}$ and the normalizations $\nu$ of step 2 send the relabelled $(x\otimes u)\otimes v$ to the relabelled $x\otimes q_{b,a}(u)v$. With step 3 this gives the asserted coherence of the comparisons with both reduction and composition.

proof.text:
Fix $b\geq a\geq1$ and $m\geq1$. Apply [lem-trf-scheme-galois-coefficient-change] with its coefficient rings $A=A_b$, $B=A_a$, quotient homomorphism, and object $K_b$. These are finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$, hence by integers prime to $p$. The finite-type finite-field scheme and the specified canonical $\kappa^{(m)}$ are exactly those of its statement. Its theorem applies on the ordinary unbounded constant-coefficient derived categories, without a flatness assumption on $A_a/A_b$. Write $T=-\otimes^L_{B_b}B_a$ and $c_h:Lh_{A_a}^*T\simeq T Lh_{A_b}^*$ for the comparison specified there. It gives
$$T(\kappa^{(m)}_{A_b,K_b})\circ c_{\Phi^m,K_b}=c_{g_\gamma^m,K_b}\circ\kappa^{(m)}_{A_a,TK_b}.$$
Use the natural normalization $\eta_{b,a}:TK_b\simeq K_a$ from step 1. For $h=\Phi^m,g_\gamma^m$ put $\beta_h=Lh_{A_a}^*(\eta_{b,a})\circ c_{h,K_b}^{-1}$. Postcompose the displayed equality with $L(g_\gamma^m)_{A_a}^*(\eta_{b,a})$ and use naturality of $\kappa^{(m)}$ at $\eta_{b,a}$; this yields
$$\beta_{g_\gamma^m}\circ T(\kappa^{(m)}_{A_b,K_b})=\kappa^{(m)}_{A_a,K_a}\circ\beta_{\Phi^m}.$$
This is the requested reduction square. The cited theorem concerns the comparison built from absolute-Frobenius trivialization and Frobenius factorization, so it identifies the actual $\kappa^{(m)}$ in the item. Since $a,b,m$ were arbitrary, every derived coefficient quotient and every stated power are covered.
